title: Name, speech, mind, will, thought — the ladder (7.1–7.5)
hook: Narada keeps asking one question, sir, is there anything greater than this? and every time, the answer is yes

segments.voice: Yesterday: atmavit, the learned sage who knows words but not the self. Your line was knowledge isn't it.

Kids discover a game early. Why? Because. But why? Because of this. But why that? It drives parents up the wall. And yet it's how you get to the bottom of things: keep asking for the next layer down. Sanatkumara has told Narada that everything he studied is only name. Narada, to his credit, doesn't argue. He asks the next question. Sir, is there anything greater than name?
screen: `WHY? BECAUSE. BUT WHY?` → `ALL YOU KNOW IS ONLY NAME.` → `IS THERE ANYTHING GREATER?`

segments.voice: The first rung is name. Revere name as Brahman, Sanatkumara says. As far as name reaches, you'll have freedom there. A fair start: names are how people hold the world. Is there anything greater than name? Yes, speech. Speech makes the Vedas known, and earth and sky, right and wrong, true and false. Without speech, right and wrong couldn't be made known at all. Greater than speech? Mind. And here's an image from the hand: as a closed fist holds two small fruits, mind holds both speech and name. When you think, let me learn these verses, then you learn them. Let me do this, then you do it. Greater than mind? Will, samkalpa, intention. When you intend something, then you think it, then you say it, then you give it a name. Greater than will? Thought, citta: attention, the awareness that notices before you even intend. And Sanatkumara says something pointed here. If someone knows a great deal but has no real attention, people say: he's nobody. If someone knows little but is truly attentive, people want to listen. Look at the direction of the climb. Name, speech, mind, will, thought. Each rung is quieter and more inward, and each holds the one below it. Narada came in with a mountain of names. Sanatkumara is walking him up and in, toward the one who's paying attention.
screen: `NAME: HOW WE HOLD THE WORLD.` · `SPEECH: RIGHT AND WRONG MADE KNOWN.` · `MIND HOLDS BOTH, LIKE A FIST.` · `WILL, THEN THOUGHT.` · then, large: `EACH IS GREATER.`

segments.voice: Notice a name in your mind, then the inner voice that says it, then the mind behind the voice, then the intention under the thought, then the plain attention that notices all of it. Rest at that top rung for as long as you can, and when you slip down, climb again.
Name. The first rung of Sanatkumara's ladder; above it, speech, mind, will and thought, each greater than the last.
Your line: each is greater. And at every rung, Narada asks again: is there anything greater? See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Teachers of Vedanta often walk students up Sanatkumara's ladder as a contemplative exercise, moving attention from words to mind to awareness.

chat.says: What's the point of Sanatkumara's ladder, from name up to thought?
options: Each rung holds the one below and is more inward: name, speech, mind, will, thought.
It ranks people: those who know names at the bottom, sages at the top.
It's a list of subjects Narada must master before he can be taught.
chat.meaning: Speech is greater than name, mind than speech, will than mind, thought than will. Each rung is more inward and holds the one below.

Narada.meaning: a famous sage, learned in every subject of his day
